name: USB Adapter

steps.text: Make sure at least one Access Point 2443 or other dual-band Insteon product is installed; the USB Adapter is RF-only.
Make sure the USB Adapter is not connected to your computer.
Download the FTDI virtual COM port (VCP) driver for your operating system, then save, extract and run it. On a Mac, mount the disk image, run the installer package for your OS version and reboot.
Plug the USB Adapter into an available USB port on your computer.
steps.expect: Status LED turns on solid green and stays on while plugged in

steps.text: Start your Insteon-compatible software and follow its instructions to add and use the USB Adapter.

notes: For the best network performance, install at least two dual-band Insteon products.
The USB Adapter communicates with the computer as long as it is connected, which may wake the computer from sleep.

The steps combine two quick start versions for the same model: the Portable USB Adapter 2448A7 Quick Start Guide, from 2010 and for Windows only, names the Access Point 2443 and gives the Windows driver; the USB Stick 2448A7 Quick Start Guide, from 2013 and for PC or Mac, adds the Mac driver steps. Otherwise they give the same steps.

steps.text: Have the controlling software send the Start ALL-Linking command to the USB Adapter.

notes: The USB Adapter has no SET button, so linking mode must be started from software.

sources: Portable USB Adapter 2448A7 Quick Start Guide
notes: Has no SET button: start linking from software with Start ALL-Linking (0x64).
Reaches powerline devices only through a dual-band device, such as the Access Point 2443 or a dual-band LampLinc.
Has no X10: it answers Send X10 (0x63) with a NAK, and never sends X10 Received (0x52).
The USB Adapter Developer Notes say it uses the PowerLinc USB 2414U's protocol, but the commands they name are the PowerLinc Modem 2413's.
